changelog: Insert a short binding rule that keeps a finite verb or light verb with the immediately following core complement, to prevent unsafe splits that separate predicates from required complements (addresses the primary finding).
findings: The prompt under-rates cuts that split a predicate from the core material that completes its assertion: it often places a cut before a verb's required complement (direct object, prepositional complement, 'by'‑agent, or clausal complement), producing high contradiction or loss.

The prompt misses that relative and clausal complementizers are unsafe cut points: it permits cuts immediately before 'which/that/who' (and similar subordinators), separating modifiers that redefine or complete the previous noun/clause and so harming cohesion or causing contradiction.

edits.now: Keep a finite verb or light verb together with the immediately following core co

diagnosis.why: Adding the short binding rule shifted mass toward earlier cuts (rank depth up at shallow depths and a negative effect in the ≤3 bin) because the insertion was implemented/parsed incorrectly: instead of merging a finite/light verb with its following complement it caused boundaries to move before or around verbs and multiword complements (isolating verbs or splitting names like “Cirque ‖ du Soleil”, “There ‖ are”, or separating verb from its object).
diagnosis.lesson: When adding this binding, ensure it actually merges the finite/light verb with the immediately following core complement (don’t invert or truncate the rule) and validate specifically on very-short pieces (≤3 words) and multiword names so verbs and complements are not isolated or multiword entities split.
